lead: a woman who sat at your bench for one afternoon six years ago has a workshop now, and her best piece stands next to yours in the same shop, and both of you find that pleasing.
sun: everything with your name on it is exactly as good as people say, and that is what brings them to the bench in the first place. they come to look at a finished thing, and the looking is honest. what they take away is not the looking. nobody arrives at a workshop that good and leaves without something, and nothing in the room has ever been arranged to decide what.
moon: The Hand cannot sit with a stuck person and leave them stuck. an hour later they have the beginning of something of their own, made in your room, out of your way of doing it, and no note is kept at either end. ten years of that and the trade is full of people whose first good day happened at your bench, owing nothing, told nothing.
pull: half the workshops in the trade started in an afternoon at your bench. when one of their owners comes for the piece with your name on it, he arrives as a peer.
tension: somebody wrote a profile of you last year and used the word influence four times, warmly, and that word is the whole difficulty: influence is what a debt gets called when nobody can produce it. so when a former visitor puts out something close enough to yours to hurt, the room reads two makers converging, and the four people who could say otherwise did the same thing five years earlier.
cost: you can put the whole of how it is done in front of a stranger and lose nothing by it, which is why the afternoon gets remembered for twenty years. the shelf under your name is large and every item on it is properly yours. none of that is a defence, and the people best placed to come for it learned to make in your room.

lead: the making has never been the difficulty and there is no second half of you where the difficulty would live — no part that hesitates at the door, no version that has ever wanted terms.
sun: a room takes very good work as evidence that arrangements exist behind it. somebody made this, so somebody must be looking after it — an agreement, a person who handles things, a line that would be crossed. the handling is casual for that reason, and nobody is being a predator. the better the work gets the more plainly covered it looks, so quality raises the assumption every year.
moon: the guarding would have to happen in a particular half-second — the thing is finished, somebody is standing there wanting it, and that is when a hand goes over it. the half-second exists. nothing occupies it. so the absence never announces itself as an absence, and by the time a year has gone past you are reading the outcome, not the moment.
pull: nothing in you was ever going to be the one that hesitated. the whole of you finishes things and shows them, twice over, and no part of the arrangement was built to hold anything back.
tension: nothing about you invites the offer. work that good, handed over with no conditions on it, reads as a person who has no need of conditions — so it gets called confidence, warmly, by people who mean it. the friend who might have stood in front of the work concluded years ago that you had this arranged, and every better year has made that firmer. the ones who do ask for something get it.
cost: a thing can be finished on thursday and be in the world on friday, entire, with nothing held back to be leveraged later, and the ease of that is in the work where anybody can feel it. no year of your life reads differently. so the difference between the piece that stayed yours and the one that did not is a fact about who was in the room.

lead: the piece is in two public collections and a textbook, and it is correctly labelled in both. the person who made it has no gallery, no faculty, no firm, and nothing anybody has ever been able to confirm.
sun: the work is good enough to be wanted permanently, and everything it reaches is somebody's building. it gets into a collection, a syllabus, a catalogue of theirs, and your name goes with it each time, spelled right and credited properly. nothing about that is theft. a made thing has to be housed somewhere, and there has never been anywhere of yours for it to be housed in.
moon: no membership was ever issued, so nothing anywhere could take a message on your behalf. no register lists you, no body would have to be told, so the work goes out with a name on it and no premises behind the name. when it needs somebody to speak for it, the nearest institution is whichever one has been keeping it, and they speak accurately, as their own holding.
pull: the work has an address and you do not. every place your name is properly credited is a place that belongs to someone else, and each of them holds a piece of you legitimately.
tension: the absence of a place gets read as a position: you turned down the post, left the gallery, chose this. it gets admired, and the admiring closes the subject before anybody asks. no decision was made. the question of where you would be based has never arrived in a form you could answer. so the help that arrives for somebody visibly stranded never arrives, because nothing about you looks stranded.
cost: work with no institution attached to it gets picked up by places that would never take each other's, which is why yours has ended up in company nothing else of its kind reaches. holding a made thing is nine-tenths of owning it in every argument that ever happens. the buildings all hold something of yours, and yours is the one address on the label with no building behind it.

lead: he has been selling your design for four years and everyone in the trade knows whose it is. in the fourth year you can still put his side of it better than his lawyer can.
sun: the design went out finished and admired with nothing on it — no terms, no registration, no sentence anywhere about what could be done with it — because the question of what could be done with it does not arrive here until somebody has done it. so ownership of the thing is settled by possession, and possession went to the one man in the trade who thought to take it.
moon: the grip arrived, and The Claws closed it on both cases at once. his is real: he put it in front of ten thousand people who would never have found yours, and no third part of you exists to rank that against the taking. so the fight will not end in either direction. conceding needs a decision and so does winning, and the same thing is missing from both.
pull: you have hold of it and will not close. the grip carries his case and yours at the same weight, and the object it was meant to be holding left four years ago.
tension: the people who love you have split into two camps and neither can hear the other. one camp wants you to fight it properly and cannot understand why a person with this much evidence keeps supplying the other side's best points in company. the other camp wants it dropped, and reads four years of not dropping it as bitterness. both are describing a decision, and the fight has never contained one.
cost: four years in, his argument still keeps its full size in your hands, and that is rare enough that he answers your letters and that people bring you into disputes of their own. the one case that was actually yours is the one you cannot finish. the design earns for him while it runs, and it runs while you hold.
